messages:
mia: Quick nsys question — trying to capture a ~200µs kernel that only appears during a KV cache eviction burst in short test runs. I can reproduce it with a full 2-min run but tiny CI smoke runs (10s) never show it. Anyone have a small/targeted capture pattern that reliably surfaces microkernels without making a 10GB trace?
rahul: Two quick tips: 1) NVTX-bracket the exact code path you care about and use capture-range=nvtx so nsys only records between your push/pop. 2) Use osrt to get thread ordering (host scheduling) — sometimes the kernel looks like it's missing but it got scheduled out so OSRT + cuda helps.
jess: Example I use locally:
```
nsys profile --output=kv-evict-run --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-end=nvtx --force-overwrite --sample=none --delay=0 -- nvtx_instrumented_binary args
```
Put NVTX around start/end of the eviction path. `--sample=none` avoids sampling blind spots (you get every API/cuda call) but trace size grows — however with capture-range it's constrained.
kai: If you can't NVTX-instrument the code, try a short rolling capture: start nsys a few ms before the expected burst and stop immediately after. I use a helper script that waits for a signal then runs `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --output=/tmp/shot` for 3-6s. That keeps files small and catches the microkernel window.
mia: @jess @kai nice. Any tips for preventing the usual "missed kernel unless run for 60s" artifact? Is it sampling bias or scheduling?
rahul: Often it's scheduling + batching heuristics. The kernel only fires when a batch boundary and KV eviction align — very low probability in short runs. NVTX bracketing + a deterministic eviction trigger (env var to force eviction) solves it. For profiling bias: avoid short sample windows and prefer event-based capture (`--sample=none`) for correctness.
jess: Also try `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --cpu-interval=100ms` if you want lightweight periodic snapshots (tradeoff: may still miss sub-ms kernels). If you need exact timing for a 200µs kernel, event capture wins.
kai: Another trick — record a tiny host-side marker (write to a tempfile) at the moment you want to capture; then run a watcher that NVTX-pushes when the marker appears and NVTX-pop after a short delay. That simulates perfect instrumentation without touching model code.
mia: Great. I'll try NVTX wrappers + forced-evict env. If it works I'll attach the trace. Thanks! :pray:
perf-bot: nsys profile finished, saved to s3://redwood-perf/traces/1732109876-kv-evict-run.qdstrace (6.4MB)
